summary: Full backend test of MNEMOSYNE Free-tier plan limits enforcement. 23/23 new plan_limits tests pass + 43/43 regression (17 billing + 26 auth_ext) = 66/66 backend tests passing. Verified /api/billing/usage structure & auth, doc count cap (10) with proper 402+detail, /documents/url respects doc cap, delete-then-upload cycle, chunk cap (200) with document rollback on rejection, chat cap (50/month) via DB-seeded messages, Pro subscription bypasses all limits, expired Pro reverts to Free and flips status='expired' in DB. Chat SSE stream still emits init/delta/done for below-limit Free users.
passed: GET /api/billing/usage (free) -> plan=free, limits={10,200,50}, percents=0, free_limits echoed, month_started_at is first-of-month UTC ISO
Free user: 10 sequential POST /api/documents/upload succeed (chunk_count>=1 each)
11th POST /api/documents/upload -> 402 with 'Free plan limit reached' and '10 documents' in detail
POST /api/documents/url when over doc limit -> 402 with same detail
Delete a doc -> usage.documents=9 -> next upload succeeds

Regression: all 26 test_auth_ext.py tests still pass
critical_code_review_comments: plan_limits.get_usage: uses count_documents with $in over ALL user conversation IDs (fetched via to_list(1000)). If a user has >1000 conversations, some chats will be excluded from the count (users could exceed 50/month). Consider joining via aggregation ($lookup) or storing user_id directly on messages so a single filter suffices — currently messages collection has no user_id field.
plan_limits.enforce_document_limit: correctly re-checks usage on every call (no caching). Uses inequality '>= 10' so exactly at the boundary is blocked — good.

server.py chat/stream: enforce_chat_limit is called BEFORE the user's message is inserted, but on success the message IS inserted. So the 51st attempt is correctly rejected without incrementing the counter. Good ordering.

server.py documents/upload rollback path (line 307): after doc chunk-count check fails, doc record is deleted but any partial Chroma writes have not yet happened (index_document is called after the check). Verified via test — usage.documents stays at 0. Good.

plan_limits.get_active_plan: side-effect of flipping expired sub to status='expired' mid-request is fine but could race with a concurrent /billing/status call doing the same. Idempotent update, so low risk.

plan_limits._month_start_iso: uses .isoformat() which includes timezone offset '+00:00'; messages seeded via test with datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() also carry '+00:00' — string comparison ($gte) works because ISO format sorts lexicographically for same-tz strings. If any legacy message was stored without TZ suffix, the comparison would misbehave. Consider normalising created_at to Z-suffix or storing as native BSON date.
billing.usage endpoint: importing plan_limits inside the request handler (lazy import) — minor overhead, acceptable, but could move to module top.

chunks limit enforcement (server.py:306 & 342) recomputes get_usage after doc.insert_one, which means the newly-inserted 0-chunk doc counts toward usage.documents but not toward chunks (chunk_count=0). Since usage.documents check already ran BEFORE insert (via enforce_document_limit), the doc insertion + subsequent chunk check + rollback is safe. However there is a small window where the doc has status='processing' and counts toward documents — if the chunk check fails, delete cleans it up. Verified.

No test cleanup fixture for the tests themselves — creates many limits-test-* users but does not delete them. Consider a session-level teardown fixture removing users with email like '%limits-test-%' from db.users / db.documents / db.subscriptions / db.conversations / db.messages after test run (matches convention used by test_auth_ext.py which also leaves ephemeral users behind).
test_credentials: Fresh isolated users per test class: limits-test-<slug>-<uuid>@test.com / pass1234. Pro subscription seeded directly into db.subscriptions with plan_id='pro', status='active', expires_at=now+30d. Expired sub uses expires_at=now-1d.
seed_data_creation: Multiple ephemeral users created via /api/auth/signup (~10 users). db.subscriptions rows inserted+cleaned for Pro/Expired cases. 50 user messages seeded into db.messages for chat-cap test then cleaned up. 60 messages seeded for Pro chat-bypass test then cleaned up. Docs and their Chroma chunks for the Pro/Free upload tests remain on disk (harmless).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Base URL from /app/frontend/.env REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Mongo access is via pymongo (MongoClient) using MONGO_URL+DB_NAME from /app/backend/.env. Pro simulation: insert db.subscriptions {id, user_id, plan_id:'pro', status:'active', started_at, expires_at:now+30d, amount:49900}. Chat-limit tests seed db.messages with created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() (must be >= _month_start_iso() which is first-of-month UTC ISO). To exercise chunk-cap: TXT with ~230k chars (chunk_size=800/overlap=120 => step 680; 230k/680 >> 200). If plan_limits.get_usage is modified to store user_id on messages (recommended per code review), the chat-cap seed logic must include user_id on each message document.
rca of the issue: N/A - no failures. All plan enforcement behaves per spec: proper 402 status, detail strings match required substrings, doc-record rollback on chunk-cap failure verified, Pro subscription bypass verified for both docs and chat, expired Pro correctly reverts to Free including DB status flip.
